content.intro: In this lesson, focus on introduction to tailwind css and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Introduction to Tailwind CSS provides the mental model needed to decide what belongs in HTML, what belongs in CSS, and how Tailwind utilities affect the rendered interface.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: What Tailwind CSS is; Tailwind CSS as a utility-first CSS framework; The relationship between HTML, CSS, and Tailwind CSS; How Tailwind fits into frontend development. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to introduction to tailwind css, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a small hero section with a heading, explanatory text and one action. Use utilities for the first pass.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to introduction to tailwind css.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to introduction to tailwind css.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: A centered content section with a prominent heading and readable paragraph; rendering requires the configured Tailwind build.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying introduction to tailwind css without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Introduction to Tailwind CSS is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
